## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Set up the graphic system you will use to present all your later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build solids you can keep editing, using move, rotate, scale and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale with nodes. Compare the solid Boolean operations and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. P2b starts: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing — units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry as points, lines, edges and faces, then build a solid you control with parameters.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a considered lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays 1 — line, grid, cube, curve

Week 6. First of two Arrays classes. Build a row, a grid and a layered array with loops and nested loops, then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction.

- [Class 06]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: Build a loop and a nested loop — a 1D row, a 2D grid, then 3D layers — then bend the row onto a curve. Name the count, spacing and index in each direction. Check your CSG print file before queueing it.

<a id="b04-second"></a>

## Arrays 2 — if/Switch in 2D and 3D

Week 7. Second of two Arrays classes. Patterns start with a brick wall where every other course shifts; then if/Switch rules make façade patterns, and the same rules, reading the layer index, make 3D patterns in an array of cubes. Hexagonal and radial arrays and math-shaped volumes are optional.

- [Class 07]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-07/) — Week 7 — Oct 6: Use Compare and Switch to select between façade patterns — a brick wall with every other course shifted is the first example — then apply the same rules in 3D, using the layer index as well as rows and columns. Start from small examples; hexagonal and radial arrays and math-shaped volumes are optional. The Blender and Rhino + Grasshopper Arrays part 2 videos are posted. No graded submission this week (studio reviews).

<a id="b04-support"></a>

## Supported practice — Arrays 1 and 2

Week 8. Supported practice, no new topic. Bring all three array sheets for feedback on repetition, index, counts and spacing, your if/Switch patterns in 2D and 3D, and anything still open before everything through Arrays is due on Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM.

- [Class 08]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-08/) — Week 8 — Oct 13: Supported practice; nothing is due. Bring all three array sheets and anything still open from 1, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1: check the loops, counts and spacing of your 1D/2D/3D arrays and your if/Switch patterns in 2D and 3D, and fix problems before everything is due on Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM. No new topic.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Attractor studies and architectural application

Week 9. October 20: teach the three attractor methods in 3.4 and their architectural application using the existing panel in 3.5. Both sheets are due together October 27.

- [Class 09]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-09/) — Week 9 — Oct 20: Attractors: compare one-point, multiple-point and curve fields in 3.4, then reuse your existing panel to design the 3.5 architectural application. Submit the two sheets together on October 27. The October 18 midterm upload remains the record for assignments 1 through 3.2.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Generative fields and the two-parameter matrix

Week 10. October 27: submit the attractor assignment and begin 4.1. Students build the 5 x 5 matrix using supplied field tools, due November 3. Point-cloud examples are supplementary.

- Class 10 — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Submit 3.4 and 3.5 together. Begin 4.1: use the supplied field groups to construct your own 5 x 5 matrix with two chosen parameters. The matrix sheet and editable source are due November 3.

<a id="b06-volume"></a>

## Architectural envelope - pavilion or small shop

Week 11. November 3: submit 4.1 and develop the 4.2 pavilion or shop envelope using field controls and optional supplied SDF Boolean operators. Plan, section, isometric and source are due November 10.

- Class 11 — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: Submit 4.1 and begin 4.2. Refine one matrix result into a pavilion or small-shop envelope within 12 x 12 x 12 m. Supplied SDF Boolean tools may assist. Submit plan, section and isometric with the editable model on November 10.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Contouring, laser-cut preparation and assembly

Week 12. November 10: submit 4.2 and introduce 4.3 contour fabrication, registration and assembly. Test before the full cut. Bring the completed model November 17 and upload documentation that night. This is the last new required content.

- Class 12 · Last new topic - contour fabrication — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: Submit 4.2 and begin 4.3. Learn contouring, numbered cutting files, registration, material tests and assembly. Complete a small test before cutting the full model. The physical model and digital fabrication documentation are due November 17.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Model submission, revisions and booklet

Weeks 13–15. Week 13: submit the contour model and fabrication documentation, and receive feedback. Weeks 14-15: revise projects, document results and prepare the booklet. No new required topic; no separate December 1 submission.

- Class 13 · Contour model submission and feedback — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Bring the completed 4.3 contour model to class. Submit the fabrication sheet, cutting files and source by 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Review the models and plan revisions and booklet documentation. No new required topic.
- Class 14 · Project revisions and booklet — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Use feedback to refine project documentation and any model issues. Review a booklet spread and the revised GSM. No new required topic or separate assignment.
- Class 15 · Final documentation and booklet support — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: Support for project revisions, final photographs, file packaging and booklet preparation during studio reviews. No new graded submission.
